name: Dumbbell Side Bend
summary: A standing unilateral core exercise that strengthens the obliques and lateral trunk stabilizers through resisted lateral spinal flexion.

setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and knees unlocked.
Hold a single dumbbell in one hand hanging at arm's length by your side with a neutral grip.
Place your free hand behind your head or resting on your opposite hip, keeping your chest open and shoulders square.
steps: Keeping your pelvis stable, bend your torso directly to the side holding the dumbbell, lowering the weight toward knee height.
Pause momentarily at the end of your comfortable active range of motion without rotating your torso.
Contract the opposite side obliques and quadratus lumborum to pull your torso back upright.
Continue past neutral into a slight side bend in the opposite direction to achieve a full peak contraction, then return to the starting position.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you bend sideways toward the loaded side, and exhale as you contract to pull your torso back upright.
cues: Move strictly side-to-side between two panes of glass.
Keep your hips square and stationary.
Pull from the opposite waistline to stand up.

common_faults.fault: Holding dumbbells in both hands simultaneously.
common_faults.correction: Hold only one dumbbell at a time so the weight provides true unilateral resistance rather than a counterbalancing teeter-totter effect.

common_faults.fault: Twisting or leaning forward at the hips during the bend.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a neutral spine and restrict movement strictly to the frontal plane without rotating your shoulders.

common_faults.fault: Swaying the hips side to side to cheat the movement.
common_faults.correction: Keep your pelvis anchored over your feet and bend only through your spine.

precautions: Avoid using excessive loads that force spinal shearing or hyperextension.
Move in a slow, controlled cadence without ballistic bouncing at the bottom of the stretch.
